list.serverListDescription: A list kept by the server.

b.label: Bans
b.description: People matching a ban can’t join.
b.overrides: A ban doesn’t remove anyone already here; kick them too. Ban exceptions override bans.

e.label: Ban exceptions
e.description: People matching an exception can join even when a ban matches them.
e.overrides: It lets them past bans (on some networks, quiets too). Invite-only (+i), the key and the user limit still apply to them.

I.label: Invite exceptions
I.description: People matching an invite exception can join an invite-only channel without an invite.
I.overrides: It overrides invite-only (+i) only: a ban still keeps them out.

q.label: Quiets
q.description: People matching a quiet can’t talk.

mask.invalidPrefix: Masks can’t start with “:” or contain commas.
mask.account: Anyone logged in to the account {account}, whatever nick they use.
mask.accountNot: Anyone not logged in to the account {account}, whatever nick they use.
mask.anyAccount: Anyone logged in to an account.
mask.anyAccountNot: Anyone not logged in to an account.
mask.mute: Mutes {parts}: they can stay in the channel but can’t talk.
mask.extended: A server-specific extended mask, sent as typed.
mask.extendedNegated: A server-specific extended mask (negated: it matches everyone the rest doesn’t), sent as typed.
mask.unknownExtban: Sent as typed: this network doesn’t advertise extended masks (EXTBAN), so it may not understand it.
mask.unknownType: This network doesn’t advertise this {prefix} mask type; it’s sent as typed and the server decides.
mask.noExtendedType: This network doesn’t offer {prefix}… extended masks, so it reads this as a nickname.
mask.matchesForward: Matches {parts} and sends them to {channel} instead.

maskUi.serverListDescription: A list kept by the server.
maskUi.inviteOnlyOff: Invite-only (+i) is off, so this list has no effect until it’s turned on.
maskUi.choosePerson: Choose someone to build the mask from, then pick what to match them by. To type a mask yourself, open Advanced.
maskUi.uncheckedParts: Unchecked parts match anything; at least one stays checked.
maskUi.accountAlone: An account can’t be combined with the others: it follows them whatever nick or host they use.
maskUi.identityMayBeUnknown: Their username and host show up once the network has told IRCord (for example after {command}).
maskUi.customMask: The mask no longer matches any of {nick}’s own parts. Check a box to build it from them again.
maskUi.maskShortHelp: A nick, or a full {mask} mask. {any} matches anything, {one} one character.
maskUi.matchesHere: No people match here | Matches {count} person here now: {people} | Matches {count} people here now: {people}
maskUi.nickExplanation: The name people see. Anyone can change nick at any time, so a nick mask follows whoever uses the nick, not a person or their account.
maskUi.userExplanation: The username (ident) their client sends. A leading {tilde} means the server couldn’t verify it.
maskUi.hostExplanation: Where they connect from, as the network shows it to everyone: an address, a hostname, or a cloak that hides it. {command} shows someone’s.
maskUi.wildcards: {any} matches any run of characters (even none) and {one} exactly one; case doesn’t matter.
maskUi.missingParts: A missing part matches anything: a plain nick {nick} is added as {nickMask}, and {userHost} as {userHostMask}. The broader the mask, the more people it catches: {everyoneMask} matches everyone.
maskUi.exampleNick: Shorthand for alice!*{'@'}*: whoever uses the nick alice, now or later. Changing nick gets around it.
maskUi.exampleHost: Anyone whose mask host ends in .example.net. Use *!*{'@'}*.example.net; on an internet provider’s hosts that can be a lot of people.
maskUi.exampleUsername: Any username ending in alice: *!*alice{'@'}* matches ~alice and alice, but also malice, from any host and with any nick.
maskUi.exampleAccount: Whoever is logged in to the account alice, whatever nick or host they use.
maskUi.exampleMute: Mutes alice!*{'@'}* instead of banning: they can stay but can’t talk.
maskUi.exampleOnly: Choosing an example only fills in the field; nothing changes until you press Add.
maskUi.accountMasksSupported: {network} also takes account masks: {mask} matches whoever is logged in to that services account. Masks without it never identify an account.
maskUi.accountMasksUnsupported: {network} doesn’t advertise account masks, so masks here only match nick, user and host, and never identify an account.
